POSTPONED PROCEEDINGS - At the conclusion of debate on H.J. Res. 140, the Chair put the question on passage of the joint resolution and by voice vote, announced the ayes had prevailed. Mr. Huffman demanded the yeas and nays and the Chair postponed further proceedings until a time to be announced.
The previous question was ordered pursuant to the rule.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with one hour of debate on H.J. Res. 140.

Rule provides for consideration of H.R. 6945, H.R. 6359 and H.J. Res. 140. The resolution provides for consideration of H.R. 6945, H.R. 6359, and H.J. Res. 140 under a closed rule with one hour of general debate and one motion to recommit on each measure.

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects mineral and geothermal exploration industries, local communities, and stakeholders in the designated Minnesota counties.
dimensions.evidence: opens approximately 225,504 acres of National Forest System lands in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties in Minnesota to mineral and geothermal leasing.

dimensions.assessment: Removes a 20-year protective withdrawal, allowing potential commercial leasing, exploration, and development of minerals and geothermal energy.
dimensions.evidence: The joint resolution removes such protections and allows such land to be leased for the exploration and development of minerals and geothermal energy.

dimensions.assessment: The source does not provide specific figures on federal spending or revenue changes resulting from the future leasing activities.
Nullifies a specific administrative rule and public land order, altering land use policy for the specified acreage.
dimensions.evidence: Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management of the Department of the Interior relating to Public Land Order No. 7917... and such rule shall have no force or effect.

dimensions.assessment: Permanently nullifies the rule, ending the long-term protective withdrawal previously established for the land.
dimensions.evidence: Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies Public Land Order 7917, which withdrew such land from mineral and geothermal leasing for 20 years beginning in 2023.

missing_information: Estimated economic or revenue impact from mineral leasing.
importance_detail.rationale: Nullifies a federal BLM order and opens over 225,000 acres of National Forest System land in Minnesota to mineral and geothermal leasing.
